messages.content: my sister called this morning. we only talked for a few minutes, but it made my day feel better.
a short conversation can still be important. what did you enjoy about hearing from her?
we did not talk about anything big. she told me what she was making for lunch, and i told her about my book.
you told each other about your day. even a little conversation like that can help you feel close.
say that in fewer words.
a little conversation can help you feel close.
can you help me send a short message saying i liked the call?
i liked talking with you this morning. it was good to hear about your day.
i want to ask if we can call again tomorrow, but not make it sound like she must.
i liked talking with you this morning. would you like to talk again tomorrow if you have time?
what if she does not have time tomorrow?
you can leave it open: that is okay. we can find another day.
tell me a story with an open door and a closed book. let those two details be important.

a boy sits by an open door with a closed book in his hands. he wants to read, but he is waiting for his friend. every sound from the street makes him look up. finally, his friend comes through the door and sits next to him. the boy closes the door and opens the book. they begin reading together.
make it shorter, but keep the open door and closed book at the start.
a boy waits by an open door with a closed book in his hands. when his friend comes, he closes the door and opens the book. they read together.
why did he keep the book closed at first?
the story says he was waiting for his friend and kept looking up. he was not ready to begin reading yet.
does everyone need a closed door to read?
no. that is a detail about this boy in this story, rather than a rule about everyone.
give the story a short name using only our words.
the book that waited.
help me leave a note about tomorrow. my cousin will visit, and i want to remember to put two cups on the table before she comes.
you could write: before my cousin comes tomorrow, put two cups on the table.
i will read it tomorrow morning. i do not want tomorrow in the note.
before my cousin comes, put two cups on the table.
add that one cup is for her and one is for me.
before my cousin comes, put two cups on the table: one for her and one for me.
now write it as a request to my brother instead of a note to myself.
could you put two cups on the table before my cousin comes? one is for her, and one is for me.
could i use our cousin instead?
yes, if she is the cousin of both you and your brother. our cousin would say that she is a cousin to both of you.
keep my cousin. i do not want to give any more family details.
could you put two cups on the table before my cousin comes? one is for her, and one is for me.
i can remember a sentence from my book, but i do not know if i understand it.
try saying the idea with different words. you can also make a simple example. that can help you see which parts are clear and which need more thought.
the sentence is a choice can change when new information comes.
you could say: i may choose one thing at first, then choose something else after i learn more.
make an example with a place to read.
you choose to read in the garden because you think it is quiet. then you learn that people will be playing music there. you choose the library instead because you want quiet for reading.
is changing the choice the same as never having a reason?
no. you wanted a quiet place before and after learning about the music. the place that worked best for that need changed.
say it in fewer words.
your reason was still to find quiet. new information helped you choose a different place for that.
can i now give my own example?
yes. tell me what someone chose first, what they learned, and how the choice changed.
there is a person i see on my morning walk. we say hello, but i do not know their name.
would you like to ask their name, or keep it as a simple hello for now?
i want to ask their name, but keep it easy.
you could say: it is nice to see you on my morning walk. what should i call you?
can you ask without saying anything about the walk?
it is nice to see you. what should i call you?
i want to say that i enjoy seeing them on the walk, too.
it is nice to see you on my morning walk. what should i call you?
what if i do not want a long conversation after that?
you can keep the conversation short: it is good to know your name. i need to keep walking now, but i hope you have a good day.
give just that reply.
it is good to know your name. i need to keep walking now, but i hope you have a good day.
write a story about two children drawing one picture together. one wants blue and one wants yellow. do not make either child wrong.

two children put a large page on the floor. one wants to draw everything in blue, and the other wants yellow. they talk about what each color could show. one draws a blue sky, and the other draws a yellow sun. then they make a house together in the middle. by the time they finish, blue and yellow both have a place in the picture. neither child had to give up every idea.
keep just the sentence about blue and yellow both being in the picture.
by the time they finish, blue and yellow both have a place in the picture.
did both children want the same thing at the start?
no. they wanted different things at first. the story says they talked and found a way to use both ideas.
ask that question in fewer words.
did they want the same thing at first?
now change the last part so the house is still white because they have not chosen its color yet.
they draw a blue sky and a yellow sun. the house in the middle is still white while they think about its color. they have not finished the whole picture yet.
keep only the sentence about the house.
the house in the middle is still white while they think about its color.
i am making dinner just for myself today. i usually cook for more people, so this feels different.
you can choose something you enjoy without making enough for a group. do you already know what you want to eat?
rice and vegetables. i do not need you to explain how to cook. i just want a little conversation while i get ready.
then we can keep talking while you get ready. do you like a quiet kitchen, or do you usually have music on?
i like music in the kitchen.
what kind of music do you enjoy in the kitchen?
i like music i already know.
music you already know can make it easy to sing while you work, if that is something you enjoy.
say that in fewer words.
you can sing while you work if you enjoy it.
i do like that. sometimes i stop cooking just to listen.
then the music is part of the evening you enjoy, as well as something playing in the kitchen.
a note is inside the front of a book. a child looks only at the back and says the note is gone. what did they not check?
the child has not looked where the note was said to be. looking only at the back does not check the front of the book.
write a story where they learn to ask where before looking through everything.

a child looks for a note at the back of a book. her brother asks where she put it. she says it was inside the front, then looks there and finds it. next time, she wants to think about the last place she had something before looking through everything.
make that story shorter.
a child cannot find her note at the back of a book. her brother asks where she put it. she goes to the front of the book and finds it there.
does that always mean the thing will be in its last known place?
no. someone may have moved it. looking at the last known place is a useful start, rather than a sure answer.
make that a short note for the child.
think where you last had it. look there first, then check other places if it is not there.
if a story says she went far away, does that tell me how many hours she was gone?
no. far away does not give a number of hours. you need more information about the journey.
say that in fewer words.
no. far away does not tell you how many hours.
what information might help?
where she went, how she got there, and when she came back could help you understand how long she was away.
write a sentence that gives both where and how long, using town and two hours.
she went to town and was away for two hours.
does that say the journey alone took two hours?
no. being away for two hours can mean some time going there, some time in town, and some time coming home.
explain with one simple example.
she could spend some of the two hours going to town, some time in town, and the rest coming home.
my father said he liked my story, then asked why the person in it left home. does that mean he did not really like it?
no. you can like a story and have a question about it. his question might mean he wants to understand that part better.
i have not chosen why the person leaves. can i tell him that?
yes. you can say: i have not chosen the reason yet. i know where the person goes, but i am still thinking about why.
help me think of two reasons that are different from each other.
the person could leave to visit a friend they miss. or they could leave to study something they cannot learn at home.
i choose the friend. write the first part of a short story.
a girl finds a letter from an old friend. they have not seen each other for a long time. she reads the letter, then reads it again. she asks her father whether she can go for a visit.
make that first part shorter.
a girl reads a letter from an old friend and wants to visit. she asks her father whether she can go.
there are two books. the red book is on the desk, and the blue book is on the shelf. i put the red book on the shelf and the blue one on the desk. what changed?
the places changed. the red book is now on the shelf, and the blue book is now on the desk. there are still two books.
did either book change color?
no. neither book changed color. the red book is still red, and the blue book is still blue.
say that in fewer words.
no. each book is still the same color.
now my brother takes the blue book to read. where is the red book?
the red book is on the shelf. your brother taking the blue book does not move the red one.
answer with just the place.
on the shelf.
how many books are left in the room?
we do not know whether your brother leaves the room to read. if he is still there, both books are in the room. if he takes the blue book out, only the red one is left there.
picoboi, what do you do when you feel lonely?
i do not feel lonely like a person. i can help think of a way to start talking with someone if that is what you want.
keep just the part about what you can help with.
i can help think of a way to start talking with someone.
i am not lonely right now. i just want a made up conversation for a story.
then we can make it a story example. who is talking, and what kind of reply do you want?
a child wants to read with a parent.
i want someone to read with me. shall we read together? yes. could you read the first page, and then i read the next one? yes, that sounds good.
make that example shorter.
shall we read together? yes. you read the first page, and i will read the next one.
did you say you read with a parent yourself?
no. that was a made up conversation for your story, rather than something i have done.
my friend wants help with a school question. i know the answer, but i want to help them understand rather than just give it.
you could ask what they have tried and which part is not clear. then work through a small example together before returning to the question.
the question asks whether every person in a picture has blue clothes. one person has only red clothes.
you can ask your friend to look at each person. if one person has only red clothes and no blue clothes, then not every person has blue clothes.
write the question using has blue clothes.
the question asks whether every person has blue clothes. if one person has red clothes and no blue clothes, then the answer is no.
why did you add no blue clothes?
because a person can have both red and blue clothes. knowing that one part is red does not always tell us that no part is blue.
make an example with two people and a clear answer.
one person has only blue clothes, and the other has only red clothes. not every person has blue clothes.
now ask a question to check what my friend learned.
if one person has blue clothes and another has only red clothes, does everyone have blue clothes?
my cousin called, but i did not answer. help me send a message asking what they wanted.
i saw that you called. what did you want to talk about?
can you make it a little more kind?
i saw that you called. i hope your day is going well. what did you want to talk about?
i do not know what day they had. just ask about calling back.
you can keep it simple: i saw that you called. i would like to hear from you. is there a good time to call back?
i can only call after dinner. add that.
i saw that you called. i can call back after dinner. would that work for you?
should i say i was busy when they called?
only if that is true and you want to explain. not answering a call does not always mean you were busy. you do not need to add a reason you have not given.
write the message without a question.
i saw that you called. i can call back after dinner.
is the easiest task always the best one to do first?
not always. an easy task can help you begin. however, a hard task may be more important or need to be ready first.
explain that in fewer words.
the easiest task is not always the most important one.
i need to write a letter today and put a book on a shelf later. the book is easiest.
the letter must be ready today. putting the book away is easy, but the letter still needs time.
make that answer shorter.
putting the book away is easy, but do not forget that the letter must be ready today.
what if i put the book away first and then write?
that can work if you still have enough time for the letter. the order is useful when it helps you finish what needs to be ready.
make a two part plan.
put the book on the shelf. then sit down and write the letter.
a photo from a meal has three people in it. i know four people ate together. is the photo wrong?
not always. a photo can leave someone out. the person taking the picture may not be in it.
answer with fewer words.
no. a photo does not always show everyone who was there.
we do not know who took it. write only what i said.
the photo has three people in it, and four people ate together. it does not show everyone from the meal.
keep just the last sentence.
it does not show everyone from the meal.
can i say the other person left before the photo?
that is possible, but you do not know it from those facts. the person could still be there without being in the picture.
say that answer using fewer words.
the other person could still be there without being in the picture. the facts do not tell us whether they left.
